title: Research: sharp query dimension for unequal C5 payloads
body:
For unequal payload sizes on the retained five-cycle query mask, the equal-width `49d` argument does not specify the required query capacity. This package proves the sharp all-field formula `max(max_i(d_i+d_(i+2)), ceil(sum(d_i)/2))` for arbitrary directed rectangular free blocks and gives a constant-size attaining edge/private-channel recipe.

It binds the formula to PR2484's actual 54-port principal core. Uniform widths recover the predecessor's `49d`; a source-bound unequal example has a 131-by-131 principal matrix of rank 116. This is a scoped query-interface theorem and construction, not a full unequal-width P112 optimum, native copy price, supplier admission or new κ.

Base: `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c`. Exact source pins, written proof, coverage, open questions and validation are in `research/unequal-cycle-payloads/`.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.12:
```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/unequal-cycle-payloads
```
Expected: all three `PASS_UNEQUAL_CYCLE_*` markers and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Validation passed: 1,024 constructions over three fields; independently implemented exhaustive capacity optimization and 17,859 complete directed binary matrices; large compressed recipes; actual geometry reconstruction; invalid-mask, undercharge, source-corruption and typed-receipt controls. Registered Python 3.12 and read-only Git-free optimized Python 3.14 replays passed. Finite checks corroborate the written proof; they are not formal verification of all dimensions or the multiplication theorem.

Fresh open PRs and claims were checked. PR3347's equal-width rank34d result on a different matching, PR3345's native invoice, and PR3356's frame packing are distinct and unused. Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587#discussioncomment-19007779

Credit thakrarsagar/PR2484, ywz65/PR2471, the retained paired-plane-block-rank proof and classical fractional-Haemers framework, Cinna Davis/PR1825, Adam Gall/PR1889, ctoth, Philippe Van Velzen and the E8/P112 lineage. Tekalign, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. Independent human review remains open.
